title.narrative: Institutional Strengthening Inter-American Court of HR

description.narrative:
Den interamerikanska domstolen för mänskliga rättigheter med säte i Costa Rica, har ansökt till Sida om finansiering om 5 000 000 SEK. Insatsen skall genomföras under perioden november 2020 till december 2021 och har som syfte att stärka domstolens institutionella kapacitet.
Stödet syftar till att stärka domstolen i dess arbete att verka för mänskliga rättigheter i regionen och detta skall ske genom åtgärder som stärker domstolens institutionella kapacitet. De aktiviteter som omfattas av stödet inkluderar 1) en ökning av antalet domstolsöverläggningar, 2) förbättrad IT-säkerhet, 3) framtagandet av en arbetsplan för utbildningsverksamhet, 4) uppdatering av domstolens policy mot sexuella trakasserier och trakasserier på arbetsplatsen, samt 5) bidra till en bredare kunskap och spridning av rättspraxis, bland annat genom översättning av viktiga domar.
Sidas stöd kompletterar andra initiativ för att stärka domstolens kapacitet vilka finansieras av Norge, Schweiz, Spanien och EU.

The Inter-American Court of Human Rights based in San Jose, Costa Rica, has applied to Sida for funding of 5 000 000 SEK for optimizing its institutional capacity to carry out its functions during 2020-2021.
The intervention aims at strengthening the Court's capacity to guarantee human rights in the region through institutional strengthening measures, which include increasing the number of Court deliberation sessions during 2021, improving security of the Court's information technology systems, formulating a working plan to strengthen the Court's training activities, updating the Court's policy against sexual and workplace harassment, and translating key sentences to other languages in order to support wider distribution of the Court's jurisprudence. Sida support is complementary to institutional strengthening initiatives supported by other donor countries, including Norway, Switzerland, Spain and the European Commission.

The objective of the intervention is to support institutional strengthening of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights to optimize its functioning in favor of fulfilment of human rights in the Americas, including the Northern Triangle of Central America. The Inter-American Court of Human Rights is an autonomous judicial institution, established in the American Convention of Human Rights in 1969, beginning its operation in 1979. The Court, together with the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, makes up the human rights protection system of the Organization of American States (OAS), which serves to uphold and promote basic human rights and freedoms in the Americas. As of now, twenty states of the Americas have accepted the Courts' jurisdiction to emit binding decisions regarding state responsibility in human rights violation cases. The Court is composed of seven judges from OAS members states, designated for a 6-year period, meeting in San Jose, Costa Rica, in periodic regular and extraordinary sessions, assisted by a permanent staff of over 70 professionals at the Court. The Court is supported by OAS regular funds (71.75%) and external donors (28.25%), executing an annual budget of 6.4 million USD (2019). Given the negative tendencies over the past few years regarding democracy, rule of law and human rights in the Americas, the Court has encountered increasing needs in terms of institutional strengthening in order to continue responding efficiently to growing threats related to respect and observance of human rights in the region.
The general objective of the project is to contribute to protection of human rights in the region through institutional strengthening of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights. The Court has identified five concrete actions to increase its operational capacity during 2020-2021 which will contribute to a creating a more robust and strong institution better equipped to respond to growing demand, while adapting to changing context and modernizing its operations: 1. Strengthen the Court's jurisdictional activity by increasing the number of sessions; 2. Strengthen the Court's information technology security, capacity and resources; 3. Strengthen the Court's training capacity through formulation of mid and long term work plan for training activities; 4. Strengthen the Court's internal policy on workplace and sexual harassment; 5. Strengthen the distribution of the Court's work and jurisprudence through translation of sentences and key decisions.
This clearly defined and results-oriented cooperation with the Court will produce a more robust and modern Court better prepared to respond to growing needs for protection of human rights and democracy in the region, and better equipped to continue expanding its donor base in the future.

During the execution of the project "Institutional Strengthening of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights for Optimizing its Capacities" Phase I and Phase II, the Court demonstrated to be a reliable partner with capacity to carry out planned activities and reach the expected results. In all 5 project objective, the expected results were achieved. Among the most important results are the following:
1. Strengthening of jurisdictional activity of the Court through increasing number of sessions
With Sida support, the Court and the Judges transitioned to hybrid working modality. Digitalization, which included acquisition of technological hardware and software, made possible to increase the number of court session to historic 29 weeks in 2021 and 25 weeks in 2022, thus improving victims' access to justice through speedier judicial processes. The hybrid modality has revolutionized and modernized the work of the Court and reduced costs related to on-site Court sessions in San Jose, Costa Rica. Sweden covered 46% of the cost of the Judges' increased workload. During 2022, the Court issued 34 sentences, one consultative opinion and tens of resolutions related to supervision of compliance of Court sentences.
2. Strengthen the Court's information technology security, capacity and resources
Sida supported important and timely modernization and updating of the Court's IT systems, improving considerably its digital security under increasing cyber attacks. The Court acquired laptops for 100% of its personnel with substantive work responsibilities, making distance work possible during the pandemic and beyond. New IT equipment was acquired also to update audio and video capacities in the Court Room for hearings and judicial deliberations. Another important achievement for institutional strengthening was the acquisition of an information security system SIEM, which provides important protection to Court files from cyber attacks.
The process for modernizing and updating the Court's digital capacities has been an important and necessary step not only for hybrid work of the Court and for improved information security, but it has also been a fundamental step towards digital transformation and the creation of a digital judicial file, which the Court has initiated with Sida support. Universidad Alberto Hurtado won a contract to develop a work plan towards creation of a Digital Court Case Management System which will modernize and transform the way the Court works. The final result of this digital transformation is calculated to take up to 4 years with a total cost of US 970,000 and is therefore out of reach of this project; however, the Sida project has made possible to plan and visualize the desired institutional digital change and modernization.
Strengthening of the Court's digital capacities allowed for improving in quantity and quality the Court's digital library which supports investigations of cases by the Legal Department and formative processes offered to different actors linked to protection and promotion of human rights in the region. During Phase I, the digital library of the Inter-American Court was created constituting one of the most specialized collection of human rights documents; 132 digital texts were acquired with Sida support. In Phase II, focus was placed on strengthening the Information and Knowledge Management Area of the Court by acquiring/renewing licences for important data bases, and acquiring digital and printed resources in order to provide better service to internal and external users. In 2022, 25 bibliographic materials, 4 specialized data bases and 2 software licences were acquired while the licence for the platform housing the digital library was renewed. All of these actions directly support the preparation of judicial sentences, consultative opinions and resolutions of the Court. Since its creation in 2021, the digital library now has 38,068 specialized resources, has received 1013 visits to the site, has 1,036 registered users and has attended over 2,000 inquires; in any given day, 772 digital texts/books are consulted demonstrating a high demand for this type of information.
3. Strengthen the Court's training capacity through formulation of mid and long term work plan for training activities
The Court has carried out training processes with relevant stakeholders since 2018 with ever increasing interest and demand. During Phase I, the Court hired an external consultant to formulate an internal mid- and long term policy document for training activities. In 2021, the Court's International Cooperation Team formulated a self-training course for the Court's Online Virtual Classroom and in 2022, six additional virtual self-training courses were designed both in Spanish and English, including: Introduction to the Inter-American System of Human Rights and the Inter-American Court of Human Rights; Access and Procedures before the Inter-American Human Rights Commission and the Court; and the Right to Equality and the principle of Non-Discrimination. These courses were offered by highly recognized law professionals from top US and Argentine Universities. The Court expected 500 people to access the courses; however, a total of 14,677 people took the courses demonstrating an extremely high level of credibility of the Court and high demand for training related to the Inter-American System of Human Rights. In 2023, the process culminated in the creation of a specific site on the Court's web site for the Training Center of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights.
4. Strengthen the Court's internal policy on workplace and sexual harassment
In 2021, all personnel received training related to sexual and workplace harassment and a small internal team was created to provide continued training on the matter. Online virtual, obligatory training course was created for staff, visiting professionals and trainees. These actions institutionalized sexual and workplace harassment prevention and eradication at the Court.
5. Strengthen the distribution of the Court's work and jurisprudence through translation of sentences and key decisions
At the start of the project, the Court had a 7 year delay in translating Court sentences into English with nearly 100 non-translated sentences, making diffusion of the Court's jurisprudence in the region and with other regional HR Courts difficult. The number of translators rose from 2 to 10, the Manual for Translations was updated, and 99 documents (from 2014, 2019 and 2021) were translated to English in 2022, reaching an all time high of translated sentences and Consultative Opinions of the Court. This result is important firstly that it gives access to the Court's jurisprudence to citizens of English-speaking countries signatories of the American Convention of Human Rights (Pacto de San Jose), secondly, it provides information to English-speaking countries of the region which have not yet ratified the American Convention and lastly, it strengthens the Courts' ability to establish fluid dialogue with the African and European Courts of HR, the UN Human Rights bodies, academy and international human rights investigation centers, contributing to harmonious development of international human rights law.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
